paper: Bertozzi, Garnett & Laurent (2012) — Characterization of radially symmetric finite time blowup in multidimensional aggregation equations

open_questions.q: For the non-Newtonian regime 2-d < alpha < 2, does the paper's Theorem-level global existence of monotone-decreasing radial measure solutions survive under numerical perturbation, and does the post-blow-up continuation observed numerically match the measure-theoretic construction proved in the paper?
open_questions.basis: The replication only exercised the Newtonian exponent alpha = 2-d, because that is where the radial problem localises to inviscid Burgers and admits closed-form shell dynamics. The paper's Theorems 1-3 (global existence, monotonicity preservation, Dirac-mass at criticality) cover the full range 2-d < alpha < 2 and were explicitly listed as C6 = out-of-scope for this replication. We therefore have no numerical evidence one way or the other for the non-Newtonian regime.
open_questions.next_steps: Implement a genuinely non-local radial solver for alpha in {2-d+0.25, 2-d+0.5, 1.5} (still monotone-decreasing radial data), compare (i) the paper's predicted global existence past blow-up against a shock-capturing or measure-valued continuation, and (ii) the mass concentration profile at criticality against the predicted Dirac component. Cross-check against the Fetecau-Huang-Kolokolnikov and Balague-Carrillo-Laurent-Raoul companion literature for benchmark profiles.

open_questions.q: How does the simultaneous-collapse prediction for the uniform-ball indicator break as monotonicity is deliberately violated? Where exactly (in phase space of initial data) does the paper's Thm 4.1 mechanism fail, and what replaces the single-time origin blow-up?
open_questions.basis: The replication verified simultaneous origin collapse to machine precision for uniform-ball and monotone (Gaussian, parabolic-cap) data. The critique section notes explicitly that the three 'independent' methods all bake in radial symmetry AND monotonicity, and therefore cannot stress-test the monotonicity hypothesis of Thm 4.1. The paper asserts monotonicity is preserved for alpha < 2, but our tests never start with non-monotone data.
open_questions.next_steps: Run the N-particle radial code with intentionally non-monotone radial profiles (e.g. annular shells, ring-plus-core, off-centre bumps under radial averaging). Track (a) whether shocks form off-origin as characteristics cross prematurely, (b) whether the local-time-to-blow-up formula t = 1/(d sup m'_init) becomes an upper bound rather than an equality, (c) whether monotonicity is transiently restored (paper's Prop.) or persistently violated. Compare against the ring-blow-up literature (Huang-Bertozzi 2012, Kolokolnikov-Sun-Uminsky-Bertozzi).

open_questions.q: For the Newtonian shock-time formula t_shock = 1/(d sup_z m'_init(z)), what is the sharp regularity threshold on the initial density rho_0 above which the observed-vs-predicted relative error stops scaling like 10^-9 (discretisation) and starts reflecting a genuine failure of the formula?
open_questions.basis: The C3 table shows two very different error regimes: rows where the observed value equals the predicted value to 10^-16 (essentially tautological because sup m'_init is evaluated on the same z-grid) and rows at ~10^-9 for d=2 that reflect real interpolation and root-finding error. Neither regime probes the boundary where the formula itself might degrade — for example when rho_0 has a Lipschitz singularity or a heavy tail such that sup_z m'_init is achieved as a limit rather than a maximum.
open_questions.next_steps: Sweep initial data with progressively rougher regularity: C^infinity Gaussian, C^0 parabolic cap (already tested), C^0 tent, Lipschitz-with-corner, Holder-C^{0,1/2}, indicator of an annulus. For each, plot (t_observed - t_predicted) / t_predicted vs. mesh resolution AND vs. regularity index. Identify where the residual stops behaving like O(dz^2) and starts behaving like O(1). This would pin down the sharp function-space in which eq. 4.5 is a strict equality.

open_questions.q: Does the density-blow-up rate rho_t = rho^2 (C5), verified as a leading-order self-similar heuristic along the collapsing-ball shell, hold universally for monotone data, or only for uniform-ball data where the shell radius satisfies r(t)^d = R_0^d - d m_0 t exactly?
open_questions.basis: The replication measures (drho/dt)/rho^2 = 1.00000 along a specific collapsing shell for the uniform-ball case in d=2,3. But rho_t = rho^2 is presented in the paper as a general density-blow-up heuristic, and the exact rate depends on how m(r,t) inherits its spatial derivative structure from initial data. Non-uniform monotone data (Gaussian, parabolic cap) were tested for shock time (C3) but the density-blow-up rate along their characteristics was not systematically reported.
open_questions.next_steps: For the Gaussian and parabolic-cap initial data of the C3 experiments, measure (drho/dt)/rho^k for k in {1.5, 1.75, 2.0, 2.25, 2.5} along multiple characteristics — inner, middle, outer — and identify which characteristics saturate k=2 and which show a modified exponent. If a modified exponent appears, compare against a matched-asymptotics prediction from the local structure of m_init near the origin (e.g. m_init(z) ~ z + c z^{1+beta}).

open_questions.q: Beyond the Newtonian case, does an analogue of the 'radial dynamics reduces to a scalar conservation law on the half-line' phenomenon exist for OTHER special exponents alpha, and if so, what is the corresponding conservation-law nonlinearity?
open_questions.basis: The paper's clever move is the exact reduction: for alpha = 2-d (Newtonian, div-free kernel gradient in the radial sense) the map m(r) = integral of s^{d-1} rho and z = r^d turns the aggregation equation into m_t - m m_z = 0 (inviscid Burgers). We reproduced this derivation independently. Whether there are other exponents alpha for which a similar change-of-variables produces a scalar conservation law m_t + f(m)_z = 0 (with some other flux f) is not addressed in the paper and would be a natural follow-up.
open_questions.next_steps: Attempt the ansatz z = r^p, m = integral of s^q rho with (p,q) undetermined, and see for which (alpha, d, p, q) the transformed equation is a genuine scalar conservation law (as opposed to a nonlocal equation in the new variables). If any additional exponent works, characterise its flux f(m) and check whether the paper's shock-time / simultaneous-collapse machinery transfers. If no other exponent works, prove that Newtonian is the unique reducible case in the radial-monotone class, which would sharpen the paper's structural picture.
